episode.title: This GIANT RHINOCEROS BEETLE Is NOT Real

synopsis: On a minimal studio desert set, a colossal rhinoceros beetle takes a performer into its mandibles, then the crew force its practical mandibles open and he steps out unharmed.

shots.prompt:
ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE, NO CUTS. A built film set reads immediately: bare studio concrete around a shallow island of sand and earth with a few scattered rocks, a tall blue screen wall with pale blue cross tracking markers behind it, a wide overhead grid of white diffusion softboxes above, and the backs of camera operators with their rigs in the foreground. One giant creature faces exactly one man. The creature's jaws open wide and close over him until he is completely out of sight inside its mouth. Crew members rush in, put their hands on the creature and push its jaws open, and in the final seconds the same one man climbs out onto the set floor unharmed, showing that the creature is a built practical prop rather than a living animal. The camera pushes in slowly from the wide establishing frame toward the action throughout, in one unbroken take.

A colossal rhinoceros beetle, its exoskeleton a glossy dark brown to black, hard and segmented, small black compound eyes, powerful pincer-like mandibles, and standing 3.5 meters tall, faces Ihsan on the minimal desert_ruins_set. The giant beetle's mandibles open wide, taking Ihsan completely out of sight inside its mouth. Crew members grasp the rhinoceros beetle's head and lower mandibles, exerting controlled force to manually open its sturdy mouthparts. In the final seconds, Ihsan climbs out onto the set floor, showing himself completely unharmed. Ambient sound only: crunching footsteps on sand, studio air handling, and crew commands.
